senses.definition: Two things, people, or animals that go together or are used together.
senses.example: I found a pair of clean socks.

senses.definition: To put two people or things together, or connect one to another.
senses.example: We will pair the new readers with partners.

senses.definition: A secret you enter to help prove that you are allowed to use something.
senses.example: We chose a password so other people could not sign in to our account.

senses.definition: A tool that stores and helps you use your passwords safely.
senses.example: With a trusted grown-up, we used a password manager to keep track of different passwords.

senses.definition: A fruit that is usually narrow near the stem and rounder at the other end.
senses.example: The ripe pear was soft and sweet.

senses.definition: A piece of land with water on most sides and a connection to a larger piece of land.
senses.example: We drove down the peninsula with the ocean to our right and a bay to our left.

senses.definition: The distance all the way around the edge of a flat shape.
senses.example: Add all four side lengths to find the perimeter of a rectangle.

senses.definition: A single human being.
senses.example: One person stood near the front of the line to help everyone find a seat.

senses.definition: The title for the men and women who ruled ancient Egypt. A ruler with this title is also called a pharaoh.
senses.example: The pharaoh Hatshepsut ordered the building of a large temple.

senses.definition: A trick where someone sends a message that looks real to get private information or get someone to do something unsafe.
senses.example: A grown-up helped us check whether the unexpected sign-in message was phishing.

senses.definition: A way that plants and some other living things use light energy to make sugars. Most plants use water and carbon dioxide to do this.
senses.example: Leaves use sunlight for photosynthesis.

senses.definition: Something so easy it takes little effort.
senses.example: After we practiced all week, the first round was a piece of cake.

senses.definition: How high or low a sound seems.
senses.example: The whistle had a higher pitch than the drum.

senses.definition: To throw a ball toward someone who will try to hit it.
senses.example: We took turns pitching the ball during baseball practice.

senses.definition: A large, nearly round object in space that travels around a star or the remains of a star. Planets in our solar system have cleared most other objects from their paths.
senses.example: Mars is a planet with a rocky surface.

senses.definition: The tiny grains that seed plants make and move by wind, animals, or other means. The grains carry cells that help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Yellow pollen stuck to the bumblebee’s legs.

senses.definition: The moving of pollen to a part of a plant that can receive it, a step that can help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Bees help with pollination when they carry pollen from flower to flower.

senses.definition: An animal that carries pollen so it can reach the part of a plant that receives it.
senses.example: A butterfly can be a pollinator when it visits a flower for food.

senses.definition: A picture made to show a person, often their face.
senses.example: I painted a portrait of my sister sitting near the window.

senses.definition: A broad area of grassland, often with very few trees. The name is used especially for grasslands in central North America.
senses.example: In summer, wildflowers dotted the tall grass of the prairie.

senses.definition: Before, or earlier than.
senses.example: To preview a movie is to see some or all of it before most people can.

senses.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
senses.example: Our weather chart shows how much precipitation fell overnight.

senses.definition: To say what you think will happen, often based on patterns or other clues.
senses.example: I predict that the ice cube near the window will melt first.

senses.definition: A word part added at the beginning of another word or word part that helps change its meaning.
senses.example: The prefix re- in rebuild shows that the building happens again.

senses.definition: Making art by transferring a design from a surface, like a block or plate, to paper, cloth, or another surface.
senses.example: In printmaking class we pressed our inked blocks onto paper to make several copies.

senses.definition: A way to show the curved surface of Earth on a flat map. Each way changes some distances, shapes, or sizes.
senses.example: The map’s projection made Greenland look bigger compared with Africa than it really is.

senses.definition: An image that light sends onto a screen, wall, or other surface.
senses.example: We watched the projection of the photos on the classroom wall.

senses.definition: A wheel with a groove along its edge that guides a rope or cable.
senses.example: The rope passed over a pulley so we could pull down to lift the flag.
